vulnerable_statements.reason: The oplock_info pointer is fetched under rcu_read_lock() but no reference is taken (no opinfo_get / refcount increment). After rcu_read_unlock() the pointer is kept and used later.

opinfo is dereferenced after the RCU read-side critical section ended. A concurrent oplock/lease break, close or durable-handle teardown from another connection can free the opinfo in the meantime, which makes this a use-after-free.
opinfo->o_lease (and opinfo->o_lease->state in the debug print above it) is read from an object that may already have been freed, so freed kernel memory can be copied into the network response.

suggested_fix: Take a real reference to the oplock instead of relying on a bare RCU pointer. For example, use opinfo_get(fp) (an atomic_inc_not_zero on opinfo->refcount under RCU), read the level, lease flag and lease state, and build the lease context while holding that reference, then drop it with opinfo_put() before returning. Another option is to copy every field you need (level, is_lease, lease state/key) inside the rcu_read_lock section and never touch opinfo after rcu_read_unlock().
